entry: Trust is in headers on a socket. Anything running as the owner's Unix user on Spark 2 can open api.sock, send Tailscale-User-Login: <owner> with no X-Forwarded-For, and be the owner: the Sparks'-own-address rule only fires when X-Forwarded-For is non-empty (24-handler.mjs:43-44). Only passkey-gated page changes stay out of reach. The installer and open-to-internet.sh use exactly this path (curl --unix-socket). The contract lists 'No Keeper' as a gap (docs/contract.md section 12); this matters for self-update and any free work run on Spark 2.

entry: passkeyGate covers page routes only. POST /actions/<name> (24-handler.mjs:224-229), /mcp (line 102) and /v1 (line 118) return before or never match it, so the owner's identity alone (including a terminal session from the internet) runs any action. What protects changes there is inside runAction and the choices code (other slices), for example owner-only questions answered only via 'page' (14-chats.mjs:85).

entry: Code and contract disagree on a missing passkey record. Contract 8.7: once a passkey exists the gates fail closed if the record goes missing. Code: a missing or empty passkeys.json means no passkey is needed (22-passkey.mjs:155-156); only an unreadable file fails closed (22-passkey.mjs:10). The handler comment at 24-handler.mjs:191 treats removing the file as the recovery path. There are no recovery codes in the code.

entry: The code asks for the passkey in more cases than contract 8.7 lists ('nothing else needs the passkey'): adding or changing a member, approving a request, saving the invite link, creating an agent key, switching an agent to look-only as well as to act, resuming agents or changing selfHeal, deploys with allowRemoteCode, adding or removing a passkey (22-passkey.mjs:110-129).

entry: mayNeedPasskey is wider than needsPasskey: /stop, /workflows/validate and /rollback are in the first but never need a passkey (22-passkey.mjs:98-99 versus 110-129), and describeChange still has wording for validate and rollback. A new gated route added to only one of the two is silently not gated.

entry: PUBLIC_ROUTES only affects requestGate. A path listed there still gets 401 unless its branch sits above 24-handler.mjs:99, and from a Spark's own address even public routes are 403 (only /health and /v1/ get through).

entry: On the tailnet /v1 needs no agent key: any listed identity with chat, owner or member, can call the models (24-handler.mjs:117-118). A key matters only when there is no Tailscale identity. A tailnet owner call may start a model on a call; a Funnel agent key needs fleet:act for that (15-routes.mjs:174).

entry: The test suite talks to the TCP port with a stand-in identity (SPARK_CONSOLE_DEV_LOGIN, test/start-mock.mjs:153), so it exercises the unlocked TCP mode. The locked mode production runs in (api-locked present) is only asserted as false (test/fleet.test.mjs:34). checkRoute, refreshBlocked, the cloud push and the backup timers do not run under ALL_LOCAL unless a test switch is set (23-http.mjs:64,90,126; 25-backup-and-start.mjs:33).

entry: Three listeners share one handler; the only differences are req.viaDoor and whether req.socket.remoteAddress is empty (24-handler.mjs:37). WebSocket upgrades do not go through handler at all: 21-editor.mjs:75-85 repeats the gate, so a new gate step must be added there too.

entry: Stale comments describe an earlier design. 01-setup.mjs:2-4,62-63 say the Sparks and users come from 'the portal'; refreshNodes only reads access.json and nothing in the service writes ownerLogin or nodes. 20-mcp.mjs:4-6 says a key only works with its owner's Tailscale identity and is read-only; keyViewer (20-mcp.mjs:34) accepts a key alone and scopes include fleet:act. deploy/cutover.sh:55 says the console copies the owner from the portal; no such code exists.

entry: Contract 4.1 and 4.4 promise an approval link for passkey steps from a terminal or agent. The code has none: tools/console.mjs:48-49 tells the owner to start it on the page, and test/passkey.test.mjs:230 asserts the old relay routes are 404. Contract section 17 itself says there are no approve links.

entry: Members exist in the code (roles, permissions, presets, requests, public asks) although contract 2.1 says there is one user; 2.1 and section 13 say to leave them untouched. Members can read the whole fleet (status, models, recipes, jobs they started, metrics stream) by design (03-identity.mjs:180-183).

entry: The viewer object is built in six places (03-identity.mjs:175; 22-sessions.mjs:75; 20-mcp.mjs:40; 14-chats.mjs:140; 18-workflows.mjs:274; 20-heal.mjs:18). The login's letter case differs by path: viewerForLogin passes the header's spelling through, sessionViewer uses access.json's, and chats match login exactly (14-chats.mjs:35), so the same owner under a different spelling sees a different chat list.

entry: readBody's size limit is first-caller-wins (23-http.mjs:8). After passkeyGate has read a body, the smaller limits written in routes are dead (for example /agents/settings asks for 2000 at 24-handler.mjs:236 but the gate already allowed 4000).

entry: Everything in flight for sign-in lives in memory: confirm challenges, sign-in challenges (HMAC key made at start-up) and device codes. Every restart, so every install or self-update, cancels them; sessions, passkeys and agent keys survive.

entry: sameOrigin returns true when there is no Origin header (03-identity.mjs:226). Page routes add an explicit 'Origin must be present' (24-handler.mjs:111); sign-in routes, /access/ask, /public/ask, /mcp and /v1 do not. Programs such as tools/console.mjs simply send Origin themselves: the check stops browsers, not programs.

entry: The daily backup includes api-locked and door.json along with passkeys, sessions, agent keys (hashes), access and the audit log; only sockets, door/ and cloud.json are left out (25-backup-and-start.mjs:12). A restore therefore also restores the TCP lock.
entry: authProblem is one module-level variable (02-ssh.mjs:69) written by every request's identity check and read for the 401 text; it carries only wording, not a decision.

entry: The session cookie's Path=/console/api does not separate ports, so it also reaches whatever is served on the same hostname's port 443 (noted as the one open review finding at docs/contract.md:1345). Hosting other apps on that hostname inherits this.

entry: service/config.json today lists four nodes (spark1 to spark4, spark2 local) with modelsHost spark3 and origin https://akspark2…:8443; EDITOR_PORTS defaults are hard-coded for spark1 to spark4 (21-editor.mjs:6).

entry: Critical files for any change to how requests get in: /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/24-handler.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/03-identity.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/22-passkey.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/22-sessions.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/23-http.mjs (with 25-backup-and-start.mjs for listeners and 21-editor.mjs for the upgrade path).

sensing: There is no single 'online'. Six things say it, from different probes with different limits: the status round (worker call, 25 s; drives events, the public page, fleet_status), inventory (scan, 45 s; drives plans, healing, what should run), the link scan (20 s), the live reader (stream alive), the offline memory knownOffline (drives /health sparksOnline and the backup target), and knowledge.sparks.online. They can disagree for a minute or more.

sensing: There is no single list of containers either. Docker on each Spark is the truth; the service holds six views of different ages: worker status runningContainers (30 s), the watcher's knowledge (60 s), inventory's labelled deployments and outside model servers (fresh, or 15 s through recentInventory), worker workloads (fresh, or 10 s), the planner's GPU-users probe (fresh), Sparkie's own status (fresh, or 5 s).

sensing: An offline Spark freezes in the watcher: a failed look changes nothing (19-watcher.mjs:74), so its containers stay 'running: true' in knowledge. The workloads action reports observedAt as the newest look at any Spark (16-actions.mjs:783), and fleetNotes lists them under 'Containers running now' (19-watcher.mjs:183-186, :193). Only each workload's own lastSeenAt shows the age.

sensing: inventory() has no cache and is heavy (du on every model folder, a curl per candidate port, on every Spark). Many page and change paths call it directly. If a scan passes its 45 s limit it counts as a miss; two in a row mark that Spark offline for a minute for everything, including a put-back's docker commands (02-ssh.mjs:60, :36; 05-library.mjs:82).

sensing: One failed status call is enough to mark a Spark 'unreachable' and write spark-offline (12-status.mjs:100-102; 19-watcher.mjs:155). The two-misses rule only governs the fast-fail memory. maybeHeal then refuses to restart crashed models on that Spark for 30 minutes (18-workflows.mjs:261), so one dropped handshake pauses crash restarts there.

sensing: While a page is open, every GPU line from the live reader deletes the offline mark (04-metrics.mjs:28), once a second. A Spark whose docker or worker is frozen but whose nvidia-smi still streams can't stay 'known offline', so calls to it keep waiting out their timeouts.

sensing: worker.py is not installed on the Sparks: it is read from Spark 2's disk and sent on every call (12-status.mjs:10-11), so an edit takes effect at once without a restart. It is not in /health's build fingerprint (01-setup.mjs:17-21) but it is in every workflow's version, read once at start (18-workflows.mjs:14, :66).

sensing: The tests never run the real worker's status, diagnostics, workloads or logs: SPARK_CONSOLE_WORKER points at test/mock/worker.py, which forwards only workspace-files to the real one (test/start-mock.mjs:150; test/mock/worker.py:1-21). A bug in those four real functions passes the whole suite and the lock.

sensing: worker.py still carries the old portal's names: state in ~/.local/state/spark-portal, the unit spark-portal-editor.service, workspaces under ~/.local/share/spark-portal (worker.py:24, :134, :318). Logs are hard-wired to the container 'sparkie-main' and the unit spark-console-api.service (worker.py:220-221), so 'console' logs only mean something on Spark 2 and a brain preset with another container name isn't found.

sensing: knowledge.sparks (online, lastSeenAt, watchedAt) is saved only when a container change triggers saveKnowledge (19-watcher.mjs:175). After a restart the file's 'online' can be stale, so the first status round can write a spark-offline or spark-online event that already happened; lastSeenAt on disk can lag by hours.

sensing: The watcher's header says a hand-started model server 'is saved as a recipe' (19-watcher.mjs:5-6). The code only records a candidate: every 'learned' event has recipe:false (19-watcher.mjs:123, :134), and nothing in service/src or public/app.js approves a candidate; it is only shown by the workloads action (16-actions.mjs:791).

sensing: Code and contract disagree on cadence: contract 6.13 says one loop brings the Sparks back to the list 'every 15 seconds' (docs/contract.md:359); the code's heal pass and held check run every 60 s (20-heal.mjs:13, :155; 20-desired.mjs:86), and 15 s is only recentInventory's age limit. The contract's own later text says 'every minute' (docs/contract.md:1241).

sensing: Contract 5.12 (fleet-wide answers: every container's logs and every Spark's metrics at once) has no matching code in this slice: container_logs reads one container per call (16-actions.mjs:716-727). README.md:57-58 says copies come from 'Spark 2 first'; the code prefers modelsHost, spark3 (05-library.mjs:197).

sensing: Sensing runs against every Spark in NODES, not only Spark 3 and 4: config.json lists spark1 to spark4 with spark2 as 'local' (service/config.json nodes). Spark 2 is probed with local bash and can itself be marked offline by two timeouts (test/state.test.mjs:226-237). plan(), plansFor() and deployOptions() will plan on Spark 2; the 'never on the brain's Spark' guard is in 17-changes.mjs:385 and 24-handler.mjs:416, not in the planner.

sensing: The cable result never expires. Nothing checks checkedAt's age; a pair keeps 'full' while one of its Sparks is off (06-links.mjs:83), and the public page draws that link (24-handler.mjs:24). If the 10-minute test keeps failing silently (06-links.mjs:94 swallows errors), two-Spark starts keep trusting an old result.

sensing: events.jsonl rolls to events.jsonl.1 at 5 MB (19-watcher.mjs:32) but a restart loads only the current file's last 500 lines (19-watcher.mjs:15). Right after a roll and a restart the history is nearly empty, and self-healing's look-backs (Spark off in the last 30 minutes, power-on detection) see nothing.

sensing: Spark ids may contain capitals and underscores (NODE_ID_RE, 01-setup.mjs:66) but the Spark pages' route only matches lower-case letters, digits and hyphens (24-handler.mjs:338). Such a Spark would show in status and plans and answer 404 on workloads, diagnostics, logs and files.

sensing: inventory(viewer), fabric(viewer, …) and refreshNodes(req) take an argument they never use (05-library.mjs:80-81; 06-links.mjs:28-29; 03-identity.mjs:196). Passing a member does not narrow what comes back.

sensing: By reading, not observed: a live reader's close handler doesn't check it is still the current one (04-metrics.mjs:40-46). If a viewer reconnects in the instant between stopSamplers killing a reader and its close arriving, the old close clears the new reader's handle and schedules another, leaving two readers on that Spark.

sensing: Memory is read four ways in different units: worker status in GiB (worker.py:115-118), inventory and memNow in bytes from /proc/meminfo (05-library.mjs:52-54, :334-338), the live reader from free -b (04-metrics.mjs:4), and GPU use per process in MiB from nvidia-smi (05-library.mjs:143). fleet_status converts GiB to GB. Live samples exist only while nvidia-smi prints: a Spark with a broken nvidia-smi sends no memory samples either (04-metrics.mjs:24-36).

changing: The lock is stale for the tree as it stands. The current build id (sha256 of server.mjs + dig.mjs + passkey.mjs) is 4f371d567af6; service/workflows.lock.json names build c0789b85fa67 (written 09:35; 14-chats, 16-actions, 20-memory and server.mjs changed at 09:54). server.mjs does match its parts. The installer only checks that the lock file exists (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:26), so installing this tree as it is would make all five workflows 'untested': every start, stop, restart and find_setups refused for everyone, page buttons included, and auto-restart skipped (18-workflows.mjs:81). Run node test/lock.mjs first.

changing: 'Every change is a workflow' (18-workflows.mjs:2, 16-actions.mjs:318) is not true in the code. Only five are: start_model, start_model_across, stop_model, restart_model, find_setups. The other change actions (cancel_operation, undo_last_change, save_workflow, run_workflow, forget_workflow, remember, forget_memory, test_changes, undo_update) and the page-only jobs (main-switch/start/stop, download, add-list, spark-action) have no version and no tested or validated gate.

changing: The page's Deploy and Stop do not go through runAction (24-handler.mjs:412-472). They skip railsFor (8 GB spare at planning, the outside/routed/in-use questions, the two-Spark refusal), agentSafeSetup, the pause and runAction's audit line; they rely on the approved stop list, memoryShare's 8 GB check inside the job, and the passkey gate for outside stops. They are not owner-only either: a member with deploy permission can use them (mustUse, 03-identity.mjs:184). Page /stop has no protected-container check.

changing: pausedCheck (17-changes.mjs:31) has no exception for self-healing during an automatic pause, although runAction (16-actions.mjs:298), maybeHeal (18-workflows.mjs:246) and healPass (20-heal.mjs:139) all let it through. So after the breaker trips, a heal job is created and fails on its first line with 'Stopped: agents' changes are paused', using up one of its two tries. For a two-Spark bring-back the surviving part has already been stopped by then (20-heal.mjs:92-96) and is not started again. Found by reading; no test covers it.

changing: The lists that decide whether a caller is 'an agent' disagree. via 'api' (the owner's POST /actions) is left out of the hourly change count (16-actions.mjs:349) but its failed jobs count toward the agents' breaker (07-jobs.mjs:64), it is blocked by the pause (16-actions.mjs:298), and cancel_operation refuses it with 'Only the owner can cancel…' (20-desired.mjs:131). 'sparkie-undo' is counted as an agent everywhere. Any new via is an agent by default in each list.

changing: One change per Spark has holes. stopContainer stops the partner part of a two-Spark model on a Spark that isn't claimed (page deploy, brain switch; 07-jobs.mjs:187-194). bringBack runs docker stop and watchBrain runs docker restart with no job and no claim (20-heal.mjs:94, :128). A 'start-model' job holds no claim while it downloads and claims only just before starting (17-changes.mjs:489), so it can fail after the download with 'Something is already changing'.

changing: Self-healing can stop things, which contract 6.12 says it never does. bringBack stops what is left of a two-Spark model, then calls start_model without noStops, so the start may stop other Spark Console models on those Sparks to make room (20-heal.mjs:92-98; 17-changes.mjs:421-430). Only a model that answered a call in the last 30 minutes turns it into a question, which ends the bring-back.

changing: A two-Spark model started by download-then-start is recorded on the desired list with the Hugging Face repo as its model (job.model = v.repo, 17-changes.mjs:468; 20-desired.mjs:29), but healReason matches two-Spark parts on the container label, which is the library name org--repo (20-heal.mjs:49). Such an entry looks like 'its part is gone' while it runs; bringBack then tries start_model, the rails refuse it (17-changes.mjs:100-101), and two failed bring-backs are logged every 6 hours. Found by reading, not run; heal-more.test.mjs only covers a model already on disk.

changing: A job gets its chat, undo and workflow tags only after the action has returned (16-actions.mjs:358-363; maybeHeal at 18-workflows.mjs:276). Page jobs get the workflow at creation instead (24-handler.mjs:426). A job that never comes back as outcome 'started' is never counted as a workflow run, never validates anything and never posts to the chat.

changing: Validation only follows the functions listed in a workflow's code(). Helpers a start really runs but that are not listed (copyModel, memNow, inventory, runJob, claimSparks, the values of KEEP_FREE, HEADROOM, CONNECT_MS, the title/fix/advice text of failures) can change without a new version, so no new real-Spark validation is asked for; the build id still changes, so the lock must be redone. The other way round, worker.py and ENGINES are hashed into all five versions although no change path calls the worker.

changing: A stop cancels a running 'start-model' job on that Spark, download included, because 'start-model' is in CHANGES_MODELS (20-desired.mjs:103), although the comment above it says downloads go on. The test for that incident (change.test.mjs:617) covers only the page's 'download' job type. 'undo' is in the same set but never matches, because undo jobs carry no node (20-desired.mjs:163).

changing: Test the changes runs its steps as via 'page', actor 'owner', trusted, whoever asked for it (18-workflows.mjs:290). Started by an agent or Sparkie, its starts and stops are not subject to the agents' pause or hourly limit, and its stop steps cancel other model-changing jobs on that Spark the way the owner's would.

changing: undo_update shares the 'undo' intent with undo_last_change (16-actions.mjs:160). When the owner says 'undo' in a chat, Sparkie is cleared to run either straight away; only the two tool descriptions keep rolling back the console apart from undoing a model change. undo_update itself has no workflow gate and is open to any agent that may change things.

changing: Nothing recovers an operation cut off by a restart: it is only reported (19-watcher.mjs:19-26), and what it had stopped stays stopped. jobs, claims, pending choices, consoleStopped and the breaker counters are memory only. The drain gives running jobs 60 seconds (25-backup-and-start.mjs:76) while a start can take 45 minutes.

changing: maybeHeal does not look at the desired list: any console-started one-Spark model that crashes is restarted, listed or not. It also records the try before attempting, so a busy Spark or a refused restart uses one of the two tries an hour (18-workflows.mjs:270-279). One-Spark entries on the desired list come back by themselves only after a power-on; otherwise they stay held (20-heal.mjs:64-65).

changing: Where the contract and the code disagree, the code does this: crash restarts are immediate and at most 2 an hour, with no 10/20/40-second backoff (contract 6.12); the loops run every 60 seconds, not 15, and the list holds no recipe (6.13); the out-of-memory fix goes to 32,768 then 8,192 tokens without asking, below the contract's 16k floor (6.9; 17-changes.mjs:212); auto-restart runs while restart_model merely needs validation, and only 'untested' turns it off (6.3; 18-workflows.mjs:254-257); a validation run needs no passkey and is taken automatically by the owner's clear request to Sparkie, saved-workflow steps, POST /actions and self-healing, and an agent that may change things can take the validation choice (section 15 says the first run is the owner's alone, with a passkey); undo is refused if another chat changed those Sparks at any later time, not 10 minutes (8.9); section 15 lists four workflows, the code has five.

changing: Names mislead about where things live. consoleStopped, maybeHeal and healTries are in 18-workflows.mjs, not 20-heal.mjs. cancelCheck, waitJob and cancelJobsAndWait are in 20-desired.mjs but are used by parts 07, 11, 15, 17 and 18. Four parts share the prefix 20 and load in alphabetical order (desired, heal, mcp, memory). config.json lists four Sparks (spark1 too); only the brain's Spark is excluded from placement, and the test run uses spark1 only as a last resort (18-workflows.mjs:317).

changing: On the stand-in fleet the lock is not checked unless SPARK_CONSOLE_CHECK_LOCK=1, and SPARK_CONSOLE_ASSUME_VALIDATED=1 can count every version as validated (18-workflows.mjs:75-76). A passing suite therefore says nothing about whether the lock matches the build; only test/lock.mjs itself does.

changing: Reference, not a surprise: the files any change to this slice has to be checked against are /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/07-jobs.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/17-changes.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/18-workflows.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-desired.mjs, /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/20-heal.mjs, with /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/08-cluster.mjs for two-Spark starts and /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/service/src/16-actions.mjs (runAction) as the gate in front of them.

knowledge: The tree is not installable as it stands: service/workflows.lock.json names build c0789b85fa67 (tested 2026-11-11T17:35Z), but server.mjs + dig.mjs + passkey.mjs now hash to 4f371d567af6 (parts 14-chats, 16-actions and 20-memory were edited after the lock). On the real Sparks every workflow would be 'untested' and off (18-workflows.mjs:81), and the installer refuses (deploy/host-on-portal.sh:56-57), until node test/lock.mjs passes. server.mjs does match its parts.

knowledge: AGENTS.md:4 says 'if code and contract disagree, the code is wrong', but for memory the contract describes far more than exists. Built: one flat memory.json, at most 40 lines, four kinds (preference, correction, fact, lesson), no history of replaced lines, no source field beyond 'by'. Not built: aliases, chat summaries, 'one active record per subject with history', a Memory page (public/app.js never calls memory), nightly git, SQLite (contract 5.3-5.5, 5.8, 15).

knowledge: Agents and memory, code versus contract 5.8 ('agents never override the owner's own') and versus the comment at 20-memory.mjs:6: an agent whose key may change things can forget any line and replace the owner's line (no check on 'by', 20-memory.mjs:41-43, 58-62; test/sparkie-more.test.mjs:32 relies on it). And through ask_sparkie an agent's statement that passes memoryClear is stored with by: 'owner', because only ctx.via === 'agent' is labelled as an agent (20-memory.mjs:49) and ask_sparkie runs with via 'sparkie' (14-chats.mjs:222).

knowledge: Model servers started by hand are never saved as recipes. learnRecipe always returns saved: false; the 'candidate' lives only on the workload in knowledge.json and no route or action approves one (19-watcher.mjs:120-136). The checks for v.source === 'seen' and v.approved (11-setups.mjs:304; 17-changes.mjs:162, 172) guard a kind of entry nothing writes. The comment at 19-watcher.mjs:5-6, the workloads description and describeEvent's '(saved as a recipe)' say otherwise.

knowledge: Forums and model cards are not read. digModel reads four sources (11-setups.mjs:151-156); dig.mjs's fromText, reportIn, speedsIn, codeBlocks, htmlText, normalizeSpace and decodeEntities are exported and used nowhere. docs/recipes.md, the header of 11-setups.mjs (lines 2-5) and the page's text (public/app.js:3380) still describe forum and model-card reading. Forum, blog and reddit setups exist only as static entries in catalog.json from 2026-11-04.

knowledge: adoptRunning can file a speed under a setup that never ran (by reading; not run). 60 s after every service start it records each running model under the library's manifest engine, image and flags (09-verified.mjs:127-135); the inventory carries no engine, image or flags for a running container (05-library.mjs:36, 97-101). A model started with a recipe setup therefore gets a second entry with default settings and the speed measured from the setup's container, and bestHow ranks proven runs by best speed first (17-changes.mjs:162-171).

knowledge: audit.jsonl is write-only: no action, route or page reads it; only tests and a person do. Through the door a change gets two lines (runAction's and mcpDoor's), Sparkie's lookups get none, and a proposal made because the request wasn't clear returns before the audit line (16-actions.mjs:314).

knowledge: Where the truth lives differs by file. verified, added-models, found-setups, memory and catalog.json are re-read from disk on every call, so a hand edit takes effect at once; catalog.json (751 KB) is parsed on every recipeCatalog() call, including inside loops (11-setups.mjs:216, 233, 244). chats, knowledge and events live in memory and the file is a copy: a hand edit is overwritten on the next save, and knowledge.json is loaded with readJson, so a corrupt one silently starts empty (19-watcher.mjs:10-11).

knowledge: A first look with a failed source is stamped fresh. The comment says a look where a source failed 'isn't stamped as fresh', but that holds only when an earlier look exists; with none, 'at' is now and the model isn't looked at again for 7 days (11-setups.mjs:195-197).

knowledge: memoryPrompt can throw (readKept gives 503 on any read error except 'missing') and it runs after replying.add and outside the try/finally in sparkieTurn (14-chats.mjs:194-228). By reading, a memory.json that can't be read (permissions, too many open files) leaves that conversation 'still answering' and the person's slot taken until the service restarts.

knowledge: What a button runs, and the operations list, are memory only. After a restart every open button in chats.json answers 'expired' (pendingChoices), recent_operations is empty, and a request being carried on (conv.task) never resumes because only a finishing job triggers it. events.jsonl keeps the start/end of each operation and reports the cut-off one.

knowledge: The brain's proven run is recorded when /v1/models answers, without the test prompt other starts need (13-main-model.mjs:214-217), and recordVerified still writes an entry when the speed can't be measured (09-verified.mjs:103, 113).

knowledge: For a named recipe setup, resolveHow re-checks flags and environment but not the image's source (only proven runs get that check, 11-setups.mjs:306). sparkie: checkInput is a small subset of JSON Schema: minLength is advertised but not enforced (remember's text, save_workflow's title, ask_sparkie's message); a string with no maxLength is capped at 200; nested objects and array items of type object are not checked; unknown arguments are always refused (16-actions.mjs:35-70).

sparkie: Starting, stopping and switching the brain are page-only routes that run operations main-start, main-stop and main-switch (24-handler.mjs:545-562).
